newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BCN says won't sell control to BBA.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BCN says won't sell control to BBA.

text.p: Brazilian private bank BCN said it ended talks with Banco BBA Creditanstalt and has decided not to sell a controlling stake to the bank.

In a published statement, BCN said its majority shareholders, represented by the Conde and Grisi families, "understood that, despite favorable conditions, BCN should follow its own path independently, maximizing its recognized potential". It added that talks with BBA had "ended completely".

It also said BCN's expansion plans are being redesigned and soon the bank's shareholders would announce a new management model under which the bank would be administered by a "shareholder company, made up of BCN executives."
The statement also said the new management model should be in place in a maximum period of six months.
After months of market speculation, BCN confirmed only in December its was holding talks to sell a controlling stake to Banco BBA, noting that negotiations would last 30 to 45 days.
Newspapers had said the acquisition of BCN by BBA would put an end to BCN president Pedro Conde's troubles to find a successor to run the day-to-day operations of the bank.
The deal would also create the sixth largest private bank.
Last year, BCN merged with local bank Banco Itamarati.
